subject: Service guarantee allowance & monthly recompense — proposal and exceptions
messages:
From: Jared Liu <jared.liu@horizoncorp.example>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@horizoncorp.example>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: SLA ask for pilot — uptime band and monthly recompense

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Horizon is excited about the throughput and latency on your hosted offering. Before we move into pilot procurement, our legal/procurement team asked if you can relax the standard uptime anchor for the first 90 days of the pilot.

Specifically, we're proposing: 
- Acceptable uptime during the pilot: 99.90% (vs standard 99.95%) with a clear carveout for planned batch training windows that may impact tail latency.
- Monthly compensation for any remedy: capped at the greater of $10k or 8% of the monthly invoice (whichever is lower).

We're open to documentation and a short exception window so we can get going, but procurement wants the concession written into the SLA amendment. I've attached our internal uptime report and an example amendment for reference.

Can your team review and let me know whether Redwood can agree to a temporary allowance and the proposed monthly recompense cap?

Best,
Jared

[attachment: uptime_report_June.csv (text/csv)]
[attachment: Horizon_SLA_Amendment_draft.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jared Liu <jared.liu@horizoncorp.example>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA ask for pilot — uptime band and monthly recompense

Hi Jared — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. We appreciate Horizon's urgency to start the pilot.

High-level response: we can consider a time-limited concession for the pilot, but we need to balance reliability guarantees and customer experience. Two immediate asks from our side:

1) Define the duration and scope of the concession (you suggested 90 days; we need start/end dates and explicit description of which workloads are eligible).
2) Agree an objective monitoring and alerting configuration (we need to be able to measure any violation consistently using our telemetry).

Proposed compromise from Redwood for the pilot period (draft):
- Pilot allowance: uptime 99.90% for the first 90 days of the pilot, but only for batch-heavy endpoints pre-identified in the mutual-action-plan.
- Remedy: monthly monetary recompense up to the lesser of 6% of monthly invoice or $8,000, with a hard cap of $8,000 for any single month.
- Exceptions: pre-scheduled maintenance windows and documented third-party provider outages excluded.

I'll loop in Ben and Laura to confirm the commercial impact and finalize wording. I've attached a slim amendment (PDF) that reflects the language above. If that aligns, we can route for internal approvals and DocuSign.

Next steps: Ben/Laura — can you please review the proposed numeric cap and confirm we can commit to the 90-day pilot allowance?

Thanks,
Mina

[attachment: Horizon_SLA_Amendment_v2.pdf (application/pdf)]

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service guarantee allowance & monthly recompense — proposal and exceptions

Thanks for the draft, Mina. Quick internal framing on commercial risk and suggested guardrails:

- Risk: moving the uptime anchor from 99.95 -> 99.90 materially increases expected monthly downtime for high-throughput customers; we should limit exposure with a strict cap and a short pilot window.

- Suggested numeric tweak: keep the 90-day concession but set the remedy at the lesser of (a) 5% of monthly invoice or (b) $7,500. That reduces our upside while still offering meaningful recompense.

- Operational guardrail: require Horizon to provide an initial list of endpoints and an estimated batch schedule (calendar windows) that we will exclude from SLO calculations. Any unreported batch activity that causes degradation would not be covered.

- Monitoring: require a read-only view into the Horizon tenant monitoring (or scheduled weekly reports) so both sides align on SLO measurement.

If legal is comfortable with the language in the attached PDF, I'm fine to approve the concession. Marissa, can you flag any billing system constraints for capping credits at a dollar amount vs %.

Ben

--
Ben Carter
Head of Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jared Liu <jared.liu@horizoncorp.example>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service guarantee allowance & monthly recompense — proposal and exceptions

Hi Jared — looping back with Redwood's calibrated position after internal review:

1) Pilot window: we can accept a 90-day temporary allowance with the following firm rules:
   - Start date: the pilot start date will be the activation timestamp in our provisioning system (we will confirm prior to go-live).
   - Scope: allowance applies only to pre-identified batch-heavy endpoints shared by Horizon in writing before the pilot start.

2) Uptime anchor: 99.90% for the 90-day pilot window only. Outside the pilot, standard 99.95% reinstates automatically.

3) Monthly recompense: capped at the lesser of 5% of monthly invoice or $7,500 (Redwood will issue account credit applied to the subsequent invoice).

4) Measurement and transparency: both teams will use the same SLO measurement method (Redwood's telemetry feed); Horizon gets a read-only dashboard and weekly SLO reports during the pilot. Discrepancies escalate to a joint ops review.

5) Exclusions: scheduled maintenance windows (>= 48 hours notice) and verified infrastructure provider outages excluded. Any unreported or undisclosed batch runs are not eligible for recompense.

Attachment: final redline-ready amendment (we will attach to DocuSign once you confirm).

If Horizon agrees, we'll prepare the DocuSign and target signatures within 5 business days so the pilot can start the following week.

Thanks — looking forward to getting the pilot underway.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
